background: Furness Building Society is a small regional mutual based in Barrow-in-Furness, funded by retail savings from its branches in Cumbria and Lancashire and lending on residential mortgages across the north of England.
synthesis: No agency rates the society, so the figures carry the whole judgement. Capital is adequate: CET1 of 16.0% is below the peer median but leverage of 6.8% is in the top quarter, the pattern of a lender whose book is almost all low-risk-weight residential mortgages. Liquidity is the softer side, LCR of 193% below the median and NSFR of 137% in the bottom quarter of UK building societies. The direction is what to watch: since 31 Dec 2021 CET1 has fallen 3.2 points and NSFR 12 points, against leverage up 0.3 points and LCR broadly flat (figures to 31 Dec 2025). Nothing has been flagged in the last 90 days.
